newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI maps out key elements for Euro monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: EMI maps out key elements for Euro monetary policy.

text.p: The European Monetary Institute, the forerunner to the European Central Bank, set out on Thursday five key elements which it said should form the basis for a joint monetary policy under a single currency.

In a study which expanded on a report released in January, the EMI repeated its view that the future bank should target either inflation, the money supply or both as the basis for its monetary policy, leaving the final decision to the ECB itself.
But it said certain elements would be central to ECB policy regardless of the final target adopted.

"In the light of the many similarities between monetary and inflation targeting strategies applied in practice, it appears feasible, already at this stage, to sketch out some key elements that should be a useful part of any strategy by the ESCB," the EMI said.
The ESCB is the European System of Central Banks, grouping the ECB itself and national central banks in the euro area.

The EMI said the future policy-maker should set a definition of price stability, set targets against which its performance could be assessed, use a broad set of indicator variables and give monetary aggregates a privileged role in this. It should also make its own forecasts for inflation.

Admitting that there was no theoretically precise definition of price stability, the EMI noted that there had been a broad consensus among central banks "that a range of 0%-2% inflation per annum would be appropriate".

On its targets, the ECB should make announcements in advance and avoid changing the target too frequently, "as such changes would not be conducive to enhancing the ESCB's credibility in Stage Three," the report said.
The EMI recommended that the ECB should use a broad set of indicator variables to help assess risks to future price stability. These should include both financial and non-financial variables.
As examples of financial variables the EMI listed the money market yield curve, money and credit aggregates, credit market conditions, bond yields, exchange rates and other asset prices.
Under non-financial variables it listed price and cost variables, indicators of aggregate demand and supply conditions, including the balance of payments and expectations surveys.

Monetary aggregates should be given a special role, with some sort of target or other monitoring system set, the EMI said. But it added: "There should be no mechanistic monetary policy response to a movement of monetary agggregates outside these ranges under all circumstances."
The ECB should also be capable of producing its own inflation forecasts, although the ECB itself would have to decide how much importance it attached to these, it said.
The EMI said the five elements could be combined and used by the ECB in different ways.

"They would allow the ESCB the pursuit of both monetary and inflation targeting strategies and could also be used in frameworks which put high emphasis on monetary targets while using supplementary elements from inflation targeting strategies, or vice versa," it said.
